title: Constructible ordinary tensor and its normalized intrinsic completion unit
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\ge1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $W_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $W=W_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $B=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/\varpi^n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site. Use the integral bounded-constructible category $\mathcal C_E$ underlying [def-wf-weil-category].
For $M,N\in\mathcal C_E$, put $T_{M,N}=M\otimes_B^L N$ using ordinary derived tensor [def-wf-tensor-product], and $C(A)=A^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$ with its specified unit $\eta_A$ [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Let $\chi^{\mathrm{quot}}_{M,N}:T_{M,N}\to Q(T_{M,N})$ be the canonical quotient-tower map of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], where $Q(T)=R\lim_n(T\otimes_B^L(R/\varpi^n)_W)$. The integral category $\mathcal C_E$ and the integral category in that lemma coincide as full subcategories of $D(B)$ with identical reduction functors. The canonical quotient/Koszul comparison is a natural isomorphism $\rho_T:Q(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(T)$ in $D(B)$ satisfying
$$\rho_{T_{M,N}}\circ\chi^{\mathrm{quot}}_{M,N}=\eta_{T_{M,N}}.$$
Both $T_{M,N}$ and $C(T_{M,N})$ belong to $\mathcal C_E$, and $\eta_{T_{M,N}}$ is an isomorphism. For any integral arrows $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$ one has
$$\eta_{T_{M',N'}}\circ(f\otimes_B^L g)=C(f\otimes_B^L g)\circ\eta_{T_{M,N}}.$$
Thus these assertions concern the actual quotient and intrinsic completion units, including their specified normalization, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of objects.

proof.text: Obtain the noetherian, finite-dimensional geometric fibre and stalkwise invertibility of ell from weilGeometricFiber_coefficientHypotheses. Stalkwise invertibility gives invertibility of the global section ell. Apply integralStratifiedPerfectDetailed to identify the two constructible subcategories. The existing detailedFiniteComparison gives the natural isomorphism of the positive reduction functors with the specified coefficient transport.

proof.text: Apply completedKoszulQuotientComparison to a chosen complex representative of each completed-coefficient derived object K. It gives e_K:C(K) ≅ Q(K), with eta_K followed by e_K equal to the actual quotient augmentation. Choose these comparisons. Their inverses send the quotient augmentation exactly to the specified intrinsic unit. To prove naturality, precompose the proposed equality first with e_K and then with eta_K. The first precomposition is injective because e_K is invertible; the second is injective by the completion reflector universal property, since the target C(L) is complete. The remaining equality is the naturality of the quotient augmentation and the reflector unit. Thus the inverses assemble into the required natural isomorphism, with its exact unit identity.

For constructible M,N transport them by the inverse of purCoefficientModel to detailed objects K,L. The equivalence unit and isomorphism invariance, followed by integralStratifiedPerfectDetailed, show K,L are detailed constructible. Take the ordinary tensor model T and comparison tau of constructibleTensorCompletion. The comparison tau is invertible on K,L, and integralOperations_preserve_constructible for the identity morphism shows its completed tensor target is constructible. Hence T(K,L) is constructible. To identify its coefficient transport with the actual wfOrdinaryDerivedTensor(M,N), choose the existing flat K-flat representatives P,Q of K,L. Ring-isomorphism scalar restriction preserves termwise flatness and K-flatness. Compose the representative comparison for T, the derived coefficient-transport factorization, ProjectionTensorCoefficient.totalIso, the representative comparison of wfTensorModel, and the equivalence units for M,N. This gives an isomorphism from the coefficient transport of T(K,L) to the specified ordinary tensor. Transfer constructibility using the isomorphism-closed predicates. No quotient tensor/augmentation comparison is needed in this step.

proof.text: The actual ordinary tensor is now bounded constructible complete. Apply wfConstructible_complete to this object to obtain that its specified intrinsic Koszul completion unit is an isomorphism. Transfer bounded constructibility along this exact isomorphism to its intrinsic completion, using the isomorphism invariance in pbcIntegralUniformComplete_isTriangulated. This proves all three objectwise assertions without substituting a different unit.

proof.text: For arbitrary integral arrows f,g let h be their image under wfOrdinaryDerivedTensor. The definition of wfCompletion.map extends h followed by the intrinsic unit uniquely across the source unit. The completion reflector bijection applied to this extension gives eta_source followed by C(h) equal to h followed by eta_target. Reverse this equality to obtain exactly the displayed naturality formula, with no invertibility assumption on f or g.
